stage_2_story.text_en: In the Cohen family, every day follows a familiar routine. The alarm rings at seven, and the children run to the kitchen for breakfast. Their father makes eggs while their mother packs their school bags. After school, the children sit at the kitchen table and finish their homework before they are allowed any screen time. Everyone has chores — the older son takes out the rubbish, and the daughter helps set the table for dinner. The family eats dinner together at six-thirty every evening, talking about their day. On the weekend, there are no alarms. They sleep in, have a late breakfast together, and sometimes visit the grandparents. Bedtime on weekdays is nine o'clock, and the parents always end the night with a hug and a short story.
